θεοῦ· οὐδὲ γάρ φαμεν μὴ ἐκ θεοῦ εἶναι τὸν νόμον, εἰ καὶ ἔλαβε τέλος. 2 Kor 5,18 Τὸ
κήρυγμα εἶναί φησι διακονίαν καταλλαγῆς, δι' οὗ πιστεύοντες καταλλαγησόμεθα τῷ
θεῷ. 2 Kor 5,19 Οὕτω νοητέον· ὅτι θεὸς ἦν κόσμον ἑαυτῷ καταλλάσσων ἐν Χριστῷ.
οὕτως οὖν στικτέον· ὅτι θεὸς ἦν ἐν Χριστῷ κόσμον ἑαυτῷ καταλλάσσων, τοῦτ' ἔστι
διὰ Χριστοῦ. 2 Kor 5, Νῦν ἡμεῖς ἀντὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ πρεσβεύομεν παρακαλοῦντος ὑμᾶς
τοῦ θεοῦ δι' ἡμῶν. εἶτα καὶ δείκνυσιν ὅτι λυπεῖται διὰ τοὺς τηροῦντας τὸν νόμον·
ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ γάρ, φησίν, οὐχ ὑπὲρ τοῦ νόμου. ὁ δὲ θεὸς δι' ἡμῶν παρακαλεῖ ὡς διὰ
Χριστοῦ, οὗ ἡμεῖς διάκονοι καὶ ὑπηρέται ἐσμέν. 2 Kor 5,21 Ἔδειξεν ἐντεῦθεν ὅπως
λυπεῖται διὰ τοὺς τηρεῖν τὸν νόμον φιλονεικοῦντας· τηροῦντες γὰρ νόμον, φησίν,
ἁμαρτωλοὶ γεγόναμεν. Χριστὸς ἁμαρτία γέγονεν, ἵνα ἡμᾶς τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἀπαλλάξῃ.
θεὸς δὲ ταῦτα παρέσχεν· δέξασθε τὴν καταλλαγὴν ἀποστάντες τοῦ τὰ νόμιμα τηρεῖν.
2 Kor 6,1 Οὐ μόνον παρακαλεῖν ἐπέτρεπε τοῖς ἀποστόλοις ἀλλὰ καὶ συνεργεῖν καὶ
συμπονεῖν αὐτοῖς πρὸς σωτηρίαν, ἵνα γνησίως τὴν παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ δέξωνται χάριν.
294 2 Kor 6,4 Ὡς θεμέλιον ἀρραγῆ προκαταβάλλεται τὴν ὑπομονήν, ἧς ὑπούσης
εὐχερές ἐστι πᾶσαν ἐπιθεῖναι ἐντολήν. 2 Kor 6,7 Ὅπλα δικαιοσύνης δεξιὰ τὸ ἔργων
ἔχεσθαι ἀγαθῶν, ἀριστερὰ δὲ τὸ ἔργων ἀπέχεσθαι πονηρῶν, διὰ δὲ ἀμφοτέρων
τούτων δικαιοσύνη κατορθοῦται· δῆλον γὰρ ὅτι ἐνὸς ἀπόντος τὸ ἕτερον ἀργὸν
καθίσταται. 2 Kor 6,8 ∆ιὰ δόξης μὲν τῶν δεχομένων τὸν λόγον καὶ θαυμαζόντων
αὐτόν, ἀτιμίας δὲ τῶν ὑβριζόντων τοὺς πιστεύοντας· ὁ αὐτὸς δὲ λόγος καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν
ἑξῆς. 2 Kor 6,11–13 Εἰπὼν οὐ στενοχωρεῖσθε ἐν ἡμῖν διδάσκει τοῦτο ἀντὶ τοῦ οὐ
στενοχωροῦμεν ὑμᾶς τῇ σωτηρίῳ διδασκαλίᾳ οὐδὲ ἐλλείψει τῇ παρ' ἡμῶν· ἡ γὰρ
καρδία ἡμῶν πεπλάτυνται καὶ τὸ στόμα ἡμῶν ἀνέῳγε πρὸς διδασκαλίαν. καὶ ὑμεῖς
οὖν ὡς κατ' ἀντίδοσιν πλατύνατε ὑμῶν τὴν διάνοιαν καὶ καταδέξασθε τὴν
διδασκαλίαν· οὐχ οὕτω γὰρ ἥπλωται ὑμῶν ἡ καρδία ὡς δέξασθαι τὰς παρ' ἐμοῦ
διδασκαλίας. ὥστε στενοχωρεῖσθε δι' ἑαυτοὺς οὐκ ὄντες πλειόνων παραγγελμάτων
δεκτικοί. 2 Kor 7,9 ∆έξασθε λέγοντας ἡμᾶς· ἵνα ἐν μηδενὶ ζημιωθῆτε ἐξ ἡμῶν. εἰ γὰρ
σεσιωπήκειν, φησί, καὶ μὴ ἐπέπληξα, οὐκ ἐλυπεῖσθε· εἰ δὲ μὴ ἐλυπήθητε, ἐζημιώθητε
ἂν μὴ μετανοοῦντες. Χαίρω, φησίν, ἐπὶ ταῖς θλίψεσιν ὑμῶν, ὅτι οὔκ εἰσι κοσμικαὶ
ἀλλὰ πνευματικαί. μνημονεύει δὲ ἑξῆς τῶν διὰ Χριστὸν συμβάντων αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ
Ἀσίᾳ. 2 Kor 7,12 Καὶ μὴν διὰ τοῦτο ἔγραψεν. ἀλλ' ὡς ἔοικεν καὶ ὡς ἡ ἔκβασις ἔδειξεν,
οὐ διὰ τοῦτο ἔγραφον, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸ δειχθῆναι τὴν σπουδὴν ὑμῶν καὶ τὴν ὑπακοήν·
ὥστε ἑτέρου προφάσει ἕτερον κατενοήθη. 295 2 Kor 7,13 Ἐν τούτῳ ἀναπέπαυται, ὅτι
ὑπήκουον αὐτοῦ τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ. 2 Kor 8,2 Ἐν ᾧ, φησί, πάνυ θλίβονται διωκόμενοι,
ἐν τούτῳ πλέον χαίρουσιν, καὶ ἡ κατὰ βάθους πτωχεία αὐτῶν ἐπερίσσευσεν εἰς τὸν
πλοῦτον τῆς ἁπλότητος αὐτῶν. μαρτυρεῖ δὲ τοῖς Μακεδόσιν ὁ ἀπόστολος ὅτι καὶ
πτωχοὶ ὄντες δαψιλεῖς εἰς εὐποιΐαν ἐγένοντο, ἵνα καὶ οἱ Korίνθιοι πρὸς
καρποφορίαν διεγερθῶσιν. 2 Kor 8,6 Ἡ προθυμία Μακεδόνων ἡ εἰς τὴν εὐποιΐαν
προετρέψατο ἡμᾶς εἰς τὸ παρακαλέσαι Τίτον ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἵνα καὶ ὑμᾶς εἰς
καρποφορίαν προτρέψηται. διὰ δὲ τοῦτο εἶπε καὶ ταύτην, ἐπειδὴ εἶχον παρ' αὐτοῦ
τὴν χάριν τῆς διδασκαλίας. 2 Kor 8,8 ∆ιὰ τῆς ἑτέρων λέγει τῶν Μακεδόνων. 2 Kor
8,18– Τοῦτο συναπτέον πρὸς τὸ συνεπέμψαμεν τὸν ἀδελφὸν οὗ ὁ ἔπαινος ἐν τῷ
εὐαγγελίῳ, ἵνα πολλῇ καὶ ἁδρᾷ τῇ παρὰ τῶν ἐξ ἐθνῶν εὐποιΐᾳ ἀρκέσωσιν
ὑπηρετήσασθαι, περιστελλόμενοι καὶ φυλαττόμενοι, μή τις ἡμᾶς μωμήσηται ὡς
ἐμποδίζοντας τῇ εὐποιΐᾳ τῇ εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους. Ἐνώπιον μὲν κυρίου καλὸν τὸ
ὑπηρετεῖν τῇ εὐποιΐᾳ, ἐνώπιον δὲ ἀνθρώπων τὸ μὴ μωμηθῆναι καὶ διαβληθῆναι ἐν
τῇ ἁδρότητι τῆς διακονίας. 2 Kor 10,2–6 Οὐχ ὡς οἱ στρατιῶται τοῦ κόσμου ὀψώνια
λαμβάνουσιν, οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐπὶ τῷ λαμβάνειν ὀψώνια κηρύττομεν. Καὶ ἐν ἑτοίμῳ
ἔχοντες ἐκδικῆσαι πᾶσαν παρακοήν, ὅταν πληρωθῇ ὑμῶν ἡ ὑπακοή. ἐπειδὴ ᾔδειν ὅτι
τινὲς λόγῳ πείθονται καὶ παραινέσει, οὐκ ἐβουλήθην εὐθὺς ἀποτομίᾳ χρήσασθαι ᾗ
λογίζομαι ἐπί τινας, ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἐφαίνοντο οἱ λόγῳ μόνῳ ὑπακούοντες. 296 πρῶτον δὲ
pass_a_gloss:
[Continues the 5:17 note: "for whether you should say law or grace, all things are from] God; for neither do we say the law is not from God, even if it took an end.
[Label 2 Cor 5:18.] He says the preaching is a ministry of reconciliation, through which, believing, we will be reconciled to God.
[Label 2 Cor 5:19.] It is to be understood thus: that God was reconciling the world to himself in Christ. So then it is to be punctuated thus: that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, that is, through Christ.
[Label printed "2 Kor 5," without a verse number; the words are 5:20.] Now we are ambassadors in place of Christ, God appealing to you through us. Then he also shows that he is grieved on account of those keeping the law; for "on behalf of Christ," he says, not on behalf of the law. And God appeals through us as through Christ, of whom we are ministers and servants.
[Label 2 Cor 5:21.] He showed from here how he is grieved on account of those contending to keep the law; for keeping law, he says, we have become sinners. Christ has become sin, so that he might free us from sin. And God provided these things: receive the reconciliation, having stood away from keeping the legal ordinances.
[Label 2 Cor 6:1.] He entrusted to the apostles not only to exhort but also to work with and toil with them toward salvation, so that they might genuinely receive the grace from God. [Page number 294 dropped.]
[Label 2 Cor 6:4.] As an unbreakable foundation he lays down endurance first, which being present underneath, it is easy to place every commandment on.
[Label 2 Cor 6:7.] Weapons of righteousness: right, the holding to good works; left, the keeping away from evil works; and through both of these righteousness is accomplished; for it is clear that, one being absent, the other is rendered idle.
[Label 2 Cor 6:8.] Through glory of those receiving the word and admiring it, and dishonor of those insulting those believing; and the same account also about the things following.
[Label 2 Cor 6:11-13.] Having said "you are not restricted in us," he teaches this in place of: "we do not restrict you in the saving teaching nor by a lack from us; for our heart has been widened and our mouth has opened toward teaching." "And you therefore, as by way of exchange, widen your understanding and receive the teaching; for your heart has not been so spread open as to receive the teachings from me." So you are restricted through yourselves, not being receptive of more precepts.
[Label 2 Cor 7:9.] Receive us saying: "so that you may be harmed by us in nothing." For if I had kept silent, he says, and had not rebuked, you would not be grieved; and if you had not been grieved, you would have been harmed, not repenting. I rejoice, he says, at your afflictions, because they are not worldly but spiritual. And next he makes mention of the things that happened to him on account of Christ in Asia.
[Label 2 Cor 7:12.] And yet on account of this he wrote. But as it seems and as the outcome showed, "I was not writing on account of this, but on account of your zeal and the obedience being shown"; so that by pretext of one thing another was perceived. [Page number 295 dropped.]
[Label 2 Cor 7:13.] In this he has been refreshed, that they were obeying his teaching.
[Label 2 Cor 8:2.] In what, he says, they are greatly afflicted, being persecuted, in this they rejoice more, and their poverty down to the depth abounded to the wealth of their simplicity. And the apostle bears witness to the Macedonians that even being poor they became lavish toward doing good, so that the Corinthians too might be roused toward bearing fruit.
[Label 2 Cor 8:6.] The eagerness of the Macedonians toward doing good urged us to exhort Titus to come to you, so that he might urge you too toward bearing fruit. And on account of this he said also "this," since they had from him the grace of the teaching.
[Label 2 Cor 8:8.] By "of others" he means the Macedonians.
[Label printed "2 Kor 8,18–" with no end verse; the words run to 8:21.] This is to be joined to "we sent with him the brother whose praise is in the gospel," so that they might be sufficient to serve the much and abundant doing of good from those of the nations, taking precautions and guarding themselves, lest anyone blame us as hindering the doing of good toward the saints. Before the Lord it is good to serve the doing of good, and before people, not to be blamed and slandered in the abundance of the ministry.
[Label 2 Cor 10:2-6.] Not as the soldiers of the world receive wages, so do we too preach for the receiving of wages. "And having in readiness to punish all disobedience, whenever your obedience is fulfilled." Since I knew that some are persuaded by word and exhortation, I did not want to use at once the severity with which I reckon against some, since those obeying by word alone were not appearing. [Page number 296 dropped.] But first ... [continues in the next section]
pass_b_english: … God. For we do not say that the law is not from God, even if it has come to its end.
On 2 Corinthians 5:18: He says the preaching is a ministry of reconciliation; through it, when we believe, we will be reconciled to God.

On 2 Corinthians 5:19: It is to be understood like this: God was reconciling the world to himself in Christ. So the punctuation should run: that God was, in Christ, reconciling the world to himself, that is, through Christ.

On 2 Corinthians 5:20: Now we are ambassadors in Christ's place, and God makes his appeal to you through us. Then he also shows that he is grieved over those who keep the law; for he says “on behalf of Christ,” not on behalf of the law. God appeals through us as through Christ, whose ministers and servants we are.

On 2 Corinthians 5:21: From here he showed how grieved he is over those who insist on keeping the law; for by keeping the law, he says, we have become sinners. Christ became sin to free us from sin. God has provided all this: receive the reconciliation, and give up keeping the ordinances of the law.
On 2 Corinthians 6:1: He entrusted the apostles not only with exhorting but also with working and toiling alongside them for salvation, so that they might receive God's grace sincerely.
On 2 Corinthians 6:4: He lays down endurance first, as an unbreakable foundation; once it is in place, any commandment can easily be built on it.

On 2 Corinthians 6:7: The weapons of righteousness on the right hand are holding fast to good works; those on the left are keeping away from evil works. Righteousness is achieved through both, for plainly, if one is missing, the other is left idle.
On 2 Corinthians 6:8: “Through glory” comes from those who receive the word and admire it, and “dishonor” from those who insult the believers. The same account holds for the phrases that follow.

On 2 Corinthians 6:11–13: When he says, “You are not restricted by us,” he means: we do not restrict you in the saving teaching, nor by holding anything back, for our heart has been opened wide and our mouth has opened to teach. So you too, in return, open your minds wide and take in the teaching; your heart has not opened wide enough to receive the teachings I give. So you are restricted by your own doing, unable to take in more precepts.

On 2 Corinthians 7:9: Receive us when we say, “so that you may suffer no loss from us in anything.” If I had kept silent, he says, and had not rebuked you, you would not have been grieved; and if you had not been grieved, you would have suffered loss by not repenting. I rejoice, he says, over your afflictions, because they are not worldly but spiritual. Next he recalls what happened to him in Asia for Christ's sake.

On 2 Corinthians 7:12: And yet he did write for this reason. But, as it seems, and as the outcome showed, “I was not writing for this reason, but so that your zeal and obedience might be shown.” So under the cover of one thing, another came to light.
On 2 Corinthians 7:13: He has been refreshed by this: they were obeying his teaching.

On 2 Corinthians 8:2: In the very thing in which they are sorely afflicted by persecution, he says, they rejoice the more, and their deep poverty overflowed into the wealth of their generosity. The apostle bears witness to the Macedonians that, poor as they were, they gave lavishly to good works, so that the Corinthians too might be stirred to bear fruit.

On 2 Corinthians 8:6: The Macedonians' eagerness for good works moved us to ask Titus to come to you, so that he might move you too to bear fruit. He also said “this” for this reason, since they had received the grace of teaching from him.
On 2 Corinthians 8:8: By “others” he means the Macedonians.

On 2 Corinthians 8:18–21: This should be joined to “we sent with him the brother whose praise is in the gospel,” so that they would be equal to administering the large and generous gift from the Gentiles, taking care and keeping watch, lest anyone blame us for standing in the way of the kindness meant for the saints. Before the Lord it is good to serve this kindness; before people it is good not to be blamed or slandered over so generous a ministry.

On 2 Corinthians 10:2–6: We do not preach to earn wages, the way the world's soldiers take their pay. “And being ready to punish all disobedience, when your obedience is complete”: since I knew that some are won over by word and exhortation, I did not want to use at once the severity I intend against some, because those who obey a word alone were not showing themselves. But first …
notes: 2026-11-11 claude-sumfix-b3: retranslated from the locked Greek. The old English was a word-order gloss, printed bare labels ('2 Cor 7:9'), broke off in 6:11-13 ('not being more than we...') and used bracket filler. Labels one per note (5:18 to 10:6); the edition's incomplete labels '5,' and '8,18–' are given as 5:20 and 8:18–21 from the words; the 7:9 label is kept because the quoted words are 7:9 (the opening 'Receive us' echoes 7:2). No doublets in this section. Page numbers 294-296 dropped; section opens and ends mid-sentence with '…'.

choices.why: The edition's label lacks the verse number; the words ('we are ambassadors for Christ, God appealing through us') are 5:20.

The note's opening 'Receive us' echoes 7:2, but the words it quotes ('so that you may suffer loss from us in nothing') and the rest of the note are on 7:9, so the edition's 7:9 label fits. The old English put the bare label '2 Cor 7:9' in the running text.
The note quotes 8:18 and paraphrases 8:20-21 (blame, abundance, before the Lord and before people).
